subject.title: Pause blocked background Claude CLI auth probes

question: Should any five-second Claude auth-status timeout suppress background Auto probes for six hours, or should the long cooldown require narrower evidence or adaptive escalation?
rationale: The code cannot distinguish the reported Keychain-blocked child process from ordinary transient timeout causes, so the acceptable compatibility tradeoff depends on maintainer intent.

options.title: Use adaptive or narrower backoff
options.body: Apply a short initial timeout cooldown and escalate only after repeated background failures, while keeping explicit refresh and success as immediate reset paths.

options.title: Accept six-hour suppression
options.body: Keep the current rule and explicitly accept that one transient timeout can disable background Claude CLI Auto routing for six hours.

options.title: Pause for better classification
options.body: Hold the PR until the runtime can identify the prompt-blocked subprocess more specifically than a generic timeout.

recommendation.title: Use adaptive or narrower backoff
recommendation.body: Apply a short initial timeout cooldown and escalate only after repeated background failures, while keeping explicit refresh and success as immediate reset paths.

likelyOwner.reason: He merged and reviewed the auth-status preflight whose compatibility contract this PR changes.
